skill.name: content-quality-auditor
skill.description: Audits drafts, pages, and competitor content against the CORE-EEAT content quality benchmark with publish readiness checks.
skill.summary: Scores content quality and turns CORE-EEAT gaps into a publish-ready fix plan.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static path traversal and backtick matches are false positives caused by Markdown links, examples, and inline field names. Real concerns remain around the rendered fetch command, mutable remote runbook fallback, and automatic memory writes. No evidence found of prompt injection text in the scanned files.

remediation.issue: Runtime execution of a local crawler command
remediation.suggestion: Replace the shell command instruction with approved host fetch tooling, or require explicit user confirmation plus URL scheme and private-address validation before running it.

remediation.issue: Mutable remote fallback for authoritative instructions
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the required runbook and references inside the skill, or pin remote fallback URLs to an immutable commit and treat fetched text as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Automatic writes to project memory files
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before saving audit artifacts or promoting findings to persistent memory files, especially in shared repositories.
Prefer local bundled reference files so standalone installs do not need to read outside the skill directory.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Runbook Loaded as Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill makes an external runbook authoritative and tells the agent to fetch it from the raw GitHub main branch when local files are missing. This can load unreviewed future instructions into the audit flow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly says not to score without the runbook and provides a mutable remote fallback URL. The risk depends on installation mode, but the supply-chain path is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Project Memory Writes Without User Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to save audit artifacts and promote findings into memory files, including hot-cache and open-loops, without asking the user first. This creates persistent project-state changes from a marketplace skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The write and promotion behavior is directly stated in the skill contract and save-results section. The paths are constrained, so this is a persistence risk rather than arbitrary file write.

content.value_statement: Publishing weak content can reduce search visibility and reader trust. This skill scores drafts against CORE-EEAT and turns gaps into a fix plan.
actual_capabilities: Scores content across 80 CORE-EEAT checks grouped into eight dimensions.
Detects critical publish blockers for intent mismatch, undisclosed affiliate links, and inconsistent data.
Calculates dimension scores, GEO and SEO scores, and weighted totals by content type.
Marks unavailable site-level evidence as not applicable instead of penalizing the page.
Creates prioritized improvement actions sorted by expected score impact.
Supports audits from pasted text, authorized URLs, file paths, or competitor comparisons.
limitations: It needs enough content to score meaningfully, usually at least 300 words for articles and guides.
It cannot verify site-level authority signals unless the user provides supporting evidence.
URL-based audits depend on authorized access and may miss blocked or dynamic page elements.
Scores are editorial guidance, not a guarantee of search ranking or AI citation.

use_cases.title: Pre-Publish Draft Review
use_cases.description: Check whether a draft is ready to publish and identify the highest-impact fixes first.

use_cases.title: SEO Refresh Planning
use_cases.description: Audit an existing page to find weak evidence, structure, trust, and freshness signals.

use_cases.title: Competitive Content Benchmarking
use_cases.description: Compare a page against competitor content and find practical ways to close quality gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this draft against CORE-EEAT and tell me if it is ready to publish: [paste content].

prompt_templates.title: Score a URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a content quality audit on this authorized URL as a blog post: [URL]. Include publish blockers and top fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review by Content Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Score this product review against the 80-item CORE-EEAT benchmark. Use product review weights and flag any trust issues: [content].

prompt_templates.title: Benchmark Against Competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my page against this competitor page. Compare CORE-EEAT strengths, blockers, and priority improvements: [my content] [competitor content].

output_examples.input: A 900-word comparison article with no summary box and weak sourcing.
output_examples.output: The audit reports a medium publish readiness score, no critical blockers, and should-fix items for citations, summary structure, and direct answer placement.

output_examples.input: A product review with affiliate links but no disclosure.
output_examples.output: The audit marks the page blocked until the disclosure is added, then lists evidence, trust fixes, and a re-audit path.

output_examples.input: Two competing landing pages for the same keyword.
output_examples.output: The report compares dimension scores, highlights where the competitor has stronger proof, and ranks fixes by likely weighted score gain.

best_practices: Provide the full page text, target keyword, and content type when possible.
Include screenshots, source lists, or site context for items that require external evidence.
Run the audit again after changes to confirm that blockers and weak dimensions improved.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a final score when the content is too short to evaluate fairly.
Do not treat missing site-level authority data as a content failure without evidence.
Do not use the score as the only publishing decision for legal, medical, or financial content.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits content quality, E-E-A-T strength, GEO readiness, SEO trust signals, and publish readiness.

faq.question: Can it audit a live URL?
faq.answer: Yes, when the URL is user-provided or otherwise authorized and the host tools can fetch the page.

faq.question: Does it replace a technical SEO audit?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on content quality and trust, not crawl errors, indexing, or site architecture.

faq.question: How are scores calculated?
faq.answer: It scores 80 checks across eight dimensions and applies weights based on the content type.

faq.question: What happens when data is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill marks unavailable site-level items as not applicable and explains what evidence is missing.

faq.question: Can it compare against competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide your content and competitor content so it can compare gaps and prioritize improvements.
